text: The value of $\int\limits _{0}^{π}\frac{e^{\cos x}\sin x}{(1+\cos ^{2}x)(e^{\cos x}+e^{-\cos x})}dx$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{0}^{π}\frac{e^{\cos x}\sin x}{(1+\cos ^{2}x)(e^{\cos x}+e^{-\cos x})}dx$

Let $\cos x=t$

$\sin xdx=dt$

$=\int\limits _{1}^{-1}\frac{-e^{t}dt}{(1+t^{2})(e^{t}+e^{-t})}$

$I=\int\limits _{-1}^{1}\frac{e^{t}}{(1+t^{2})(e^{t}+e^{-t})}dt$ ...... (i)

$I=\int\limits _{-1}^{1}\frac{e^{-t}}{(1+t^{2})(e^{-t}+e^{t})}dt$ .... (ii)

Adding (i) and (ii)

$2I=\int\limits _{-1}^{1}\frac{dt}{1+t^{2}}$

$2I=\tan ^{-t}\left |_{-1}^{1} \right.$

$2I=\frac{π}{4}-\left (-\frac{π}{4}\right )$

$2I=\frac{π}{2}$

$I=\frac{π}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text:
Let f : N $\to$ R be a function such that $f(x+y)=2f(x)f(y)$ for natural numbers x and y. If f(1) = 2, then the value of $α$ for which

$\sum\limits _{k=1}^{10}f(α+k)=\frac{512}{3}(2^{20}-1)$

holds, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$f(x+y)=2f(x)f(y)$

and $f(1)=2$

For x = 1 and y = 1,

$f(1+1)=2f(1)f(1)$

$\Rightarrow f(2)=2(f(1))^{2}=2(2)^{2}=2^{3}$

For x = 1, y = 2,

$f(1+2)=2f(1)f(2)$

$\Rightarrow f(3)=2.2.2^{3}=2^{5}$

For x = 1, y = 3,

$f(1+3)=2f(1)f(3)$

$\Rightarrow f(4)=2.2.2^{5}=2^{7}$

For x = 1, y = 4,

$f(1+4)=2f(1)f(4)$

$\Rightarrow f(5)=2.2.2^{7}=2^{9}$ ..... (1)

Also given

$\sum\limits _{k=1}^{10}f(α+k)=\frac{512}{3}(2^{20}-1)$

$\Rightarrow f(α+1)+f(α+2)+f(α+3)+...+f(α+10)=\frac{512}{3}(2^{20}-1)$

$\Rightarrow f(α+1)+f(α+2)+f(α+3)+....+f(α+10)=\frac{2^{9}\left ((2^{2})^{10}-1\right )}{2^{2}-1}$

This represent a G.P with first term $= 2^{9}$ and common ratio $= 2^{2}$

$\therefore$ First term $=f(α+1)=2^{9}$ ..... (2)

From equation (1), $f(5)=2^{9}$

$\therefore$ From (1) and (2), we get

$f(α+1)=2^{9}=f(5)$

$\Rightarrow f(α+1)=f(5)$

$\Rightarrow f(α+1)=f(4+1)$

Comparing both sides we get,

$α=4$

text:
Let A be a 3 $\times$ 3 real matrix such that

$A⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟=⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟;A⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟=⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} -1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟$ and $A⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟=⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟$.

If $X=(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})^{T}$ and I is an identity matrix of order 3, then the system $(A-2I)X=⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} 4 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟$ has :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} a & b & c \\ d & e & f \\ g & h & i \end{array}\right ]$

$A=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow \left [\begin{array}{lll} a & b & c \\ d & e & f \\ g & h & i \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow \begin{array}{l} a+b=1 \\ d+e=1 \\ g+h=0 \end{array}$

$A=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} -1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow \left [\begin{array}{lll} a & b & c \\ d & e & f \\ g & h & i \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} -1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow \begin{array}{l} a+c=-1 \\ d+f=0 \\ g+i=1 \end{array}$

$A=\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow \left [\begin{array}{lll} a & b & c \\ d & e & f \\ g & h & i \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow \begin{array}{l} c=1 \\ f=1 \\ i=2 \end{array}$

Solving will get

$a=-2,b=3,c=1,d=-1,e=2,f=1,g=-1,h=1,i=2$

$A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} -2 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow A-2I=\left [\begin{array}{lll} -4 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$

$(A-2I)x=\left [\begin{array}{l} 4 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow -4x_{1}+3x_{2}+x_{3}=4$ ..... (i)

$-x_{1}+x_{3}=1$ ...... (ii)

$-x_{1}+x_{2}=1$ ...... (iii)

So 3(iii) + (ii) = (i)

$\therefore$ Infinite solution
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text: Let f(x) be a polynomial function such that $f(x)+f^{'}(x)+f^{''}(x)=x^{5}+64$. Then, the value of $\lim _{x\to 1}\frac{f(x)}{x-1}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $f(x)+f^{'}(x)+f^{''}(x)=x^{5}+64$ .........(i)

$\Rightarrow f(x)$ is a polynomial in $x$ whose degree is 5.

Let $f(x)=x^{5}+ax^{4}+bx^{3}+cx^{2}+dx+e$

$f^{'}(x)=5x^{4}+4ax^{3}+3bx^{2}+2cx+d$

$f^{''}(x)=20x^{3}+12ax^{2}+6bx+2c$

On substituting the value of $f(x),f^{'}(x)$ and $f^{''}(x)$ in Eq. (i), we get

$x^{5}+(a+5)x^{4}+(b+4a+20)x^{3}+(c+3b+12a)x^{2}+(d+2c+6b)x+e+d+2c=x^{5}+64$

Now, equating the coefficient, we get

$\Rightarrow a+5=0$

$b+4a+20=0$

$c+3b+12a=0$

$d+2c+6b=0$

$e+d+2c=64$

$\therefore$ $a=-5,b=0,c=60,d=-120,e=64$

$\therefore$ $f(x)=x^{5}-5x^{4}+60x^{2}-120x+64$

Now, $\lim _{x\to 1}\frac{x^{5}-5x^{4}+60x^{2}-120x+64}{x-1}$ is ($\frac{0}{0}$ form)

By L' Hospital rule

$\lim _{x\to 1}\frac{5x^{4}-20x^{3}+120x-120}{1}$

$=-15$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text:
Let $g:(0,\infty )\to R$ be a differentiable function such that 

$\int \left (\frac{x(\cos x-\sin x)}{e^{x}+1}+\frac{g(x)(e^{x}+1-xe^{x})}{(e^{x}+1)^{2}}\right )dx=\frac{xg(x)}{e^{x}+1}+c$, for all x > 0, where c is an arbitrary constant. Then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int \left (\frac{x(\cos x-\sin x)}{e^{x}+1}+\frac{g(x)(e^{x}+1-xe^{x})}{(e^{x}+1)^{2}}\right )dx=\frac{xg(x)}{e^{x}+1}+c$

On differentiating both sides w.r.t. $\mathrm{x}$, we get

$\begin{array}{l} \left (\dfrac{x(\cos x-\sin x)}{e^{x}+1}+\dfrac{g(x)(e^{x}+1-xe^{x}}{(e^{x}+1)^{2}}\right ) \\  \\ =\dfrac{(e^{x}+1)(g(x)+xg^{'}(x))-e^{x}\cdot x\cdot g(x)}{(e^{x}+1)^{2}} \\  \\ (e^{x}+1)x(\cos x-\sin x)+g(x)(e^{x}+1-xe^{x}) \\  \\ =(e^{x}+1)\left (g(x)+xg^{'}(x)\right )-e^{x}\cdot x\cdot g(x) \\  \\ \Rightarrow gg^{'}(x)=\cos x-\sin x \\  \\ \Rightarrow g(x)=\sin x+\cos x+C \end{array}$

$\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})$ is increasing in $(0,π/4)$

$g''(x)=-\sin x-\cos x<0$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{g}^{'}(\mathrm{x})$ is decreasing function

let $h(x)=g(x)+g^{'}(x)=2\cos x+C$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{h}^{'}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}^{'}(\mathrm{x})+\mathrm{g}^{''}(\mathrm{x})=-2\sin \mathrm{x}<0$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{h}$ is decreasing

let $𝜙(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{g}^{'}(\mathrm{x})=2\sin \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{C}$

$\Rightarrow 𝜙^{'}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}^{'}(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{g}{}^{''}(\mathrm{x})=2\cos \mathrm{x}>0$

$\Rightarrow 𝜙$ is increasing

Hence option D is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text: Let $f:R\to R$ and $g:R\to R$ be two functions defined by $f(x)=\log _{e}(x^{2}+1)-e^{-x}+1$ and $g(x)=\frac{1-2e^{2x}}{e^{x}}$. Then, for which of the following range of $α$, the inequality $f\left (g\left (\frac{(α-1)^{2}}{3}\right )\right )>f\left (g\left (α-\frac{5}{3}\right )\right )$ holds ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f^{'}(x)=\dfrac{2x}{x^{2}+1}+e^{-x}$

For $x\geq 0$ both terms are non-negative and $e^{-x}>0$, so $f^{'}(x)>0$. For $x<0$, $(x+1)^{2}\geq 0$ gives $\dfrac{2x}{x^{2}+1}\geq -1$, while $e^{-x}>1$, so $f^{'}(x)>0$. Hence $f$ is strictly increasing on $𝐑$.

$g(x)=\dfrac{1-2e^{2x}}{e^{x}}=e^{-x}-2e^{x}$, so $g^{'}(x)=-e^{-x}-2e^{x}<0$ and $g$ is strictly decreasing.

Since $f$ is increasing, $f(g(u))>f(g(v))⟺g(u)>g(v)$, and since $g$ is decreasing, this holds $⟺u<v$:

$\dfrac{(α-1)^{2}}{3}<α-\dfrac{5}{3}\Rightarrow α^{2}-2α+1<3α-5\Rightarrow α^{2}-5α+6<0$

$(α-2)(α-3)<0\Rightarrow α\in (2,3)$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text: Let $\vec{a}=a_{1}\hat{i}+a_{2}\hat{j}+a_{3}\widehat{k}$ $a_{i}>0$, $i=1,2,3$ be a vector which makes equal angles with the coordinate axes OX, OY and OZ. Also, let the projection of $\vec{a}$ on the vector $3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}$ be 7. Let $\vec{b}$ be a vector obtained by rotating $\vec{a}$ with 90${}^{\circ }$. If $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$ and x-axis are coplanar, then projection of a vector $\vec{b}$ on $3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\cos ^{2}α+\cos ^{2}β+\cos ^{2}γ=1\Rightarrow \cos ^{2}α=\frac{1}{3}\Rightarrow \cos α=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$\vec{a}=\frac{λ}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k}),λ>0$

$\frac{λ}{\sqrt{3}}\frac{(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k}).(3\hat{i}+4\hat{j})}{\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}}=7$

$\Rightarrow \frac{λ}{\sqrt{3}}(3+4)=7\times 5$

$\therefore$ $λ=5\sqrt{3}$

$\vec{a}=5(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k})$

Let $\vec{b}=p\hat{i}+q\hat{j}+r\widehat{k}$

$\vec{a}\quad .\vec{b}=0$ and $[\vec{a}\vec{b}\hat{i}]=0$

$\Rightarrow p+q+r=0$ ..... (i)

& $\left |\begin{array}{lll} p & q & r \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right |=0\Rightarrow \begin{array}{l} q=r \\ p=-2r \end{array}$

$\vec{b}=-2r\hat{i}+r\hat{j}+r\widehat{k}$

$\vec{b}=r(-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k})$

Now $\left |\vec{a}\right |=\left |\vec{b}\right |$

$5\sqrt{3}=|r|\sqrt{6}\Rightarrow |r|=\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ Projection of $\vec{b}$ on $3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}=\left |\frac{\vec{b}.\left (3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}\right )}{\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}}\right |$

$=|r|\frac{(-6+4)}{5}=\left |\frac{-2r}{5}\right |$

Projection $=\frac{2}{5}\times \frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}$

$\therefore$ B is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $(x+1)y^{'}-y=e^{3x}(x+1)^{2}$, with $y(0)=\frac{1}{3}$. Then, the point $x=-\frac{4}{3}$ for the curve $y=y(x)$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(x+1)\frac{dy}{dx}-y=e^{3x}(x+1)^{2}$

$\frac{dy}{dx}-\frac{y}{x+1}=e^{3x}(x+1)$

If $e^{-\int \frac{1}{x+1}x}=e^{-\log (x+1)}=\frac{1}{x+1}$

$\therefore$ $y\left (\frac{1}{x+1}\right )=\int \frac{e^{3x}(x+1)}{x+1}dx$

$\frac{y}{x+1}=\int e^{3x}dx$

$\frac{y}{x+1}=\frac{e^{3x}}{3}+c$

$\because$ $y(0)=\frac{1}{3}$

$\frac{1}{3}=\frac{1}{3}+c$

$\therefore$ $c=0$

So : $y=\frac{e^{3x}}{3}(x+1)$

$y^{'}=e^{3x}(x+1)+\frac{e^{3x}}{3}=e^{3x}\left (x+\frac{4}{3}\right )$

$y^{''}=3e^{3x}\left (x+\frac{4}{3}\right )+e^{3x}=e^{3x}(3x+5)$

$y^{'}=0$ at $x=\frac{-4}{3}$ & $y^{''}=e^{-4}(1)>0$ at $x=\frac{-4}{3}$

$\Rightarrow x=\frac{-4}{3}$ is point of local minima

text: If the solution curve $y=y(x)$ of the differential equation $y^{2}dx+(x^{2}-xy+y^{2})dy=0$, which passes through the point (1, 1) and intersects the line $y=\sqrt{3}x$ at the point $(α,\sqrt{3}α)$, then value of $\log _{e}(\sqrt{3}α)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y^{2}}{xy-x^{2}-y^{2}}$

Put $y=vx$ we get

$v+x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{v^{2}}{v-1-v^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{v^{2}-v^{2}+v+v^{3}}{v-1-v^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \int \frac{v-1-v^{2}}{v(1+v^{2})}dv=\int \frac{dx}{x}$

$\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{y}{x}\right )-\ln \left (\frac{y}{x}\right )=\ln x+c$

As it passes through (1, 1)

$c=\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{y}{x}\right )\ln \left (\frac{y}{x}\right )=\ln x+\frac{π}{4}$

Put $y=\sqrt{3}x$ we get

$\Rightarrow \frac{π}{3}-\ln \sqrt{3}=\ln x+\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \ln x=\frac{π}{12}-\ln \sqrt{3}=\ln α$

$\therefore$ $\ln \left (\sqrt{3}α\right )=\ln \sqrt{3}+\ln α$

$=\ln \sqrt{3}+\frac{π}{12}-\ln \sqrt{3}=\frac{π}{12}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text: Let $θ$ be the angle between the vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$, where $|\vec{a}|=4,$ $|\vec{b}|=3$ and $θ\in \left (\frac{π}{4},\frac{π}{3}\right )$. Then $\left |\left (\vec{a}-\vec{b}\right )\times \left (\vec{a}+\vec{b}\right )\right |^{2}+4\left (\vec{a}\quad .\vec{b}\right )^{2}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left |\left (\vec{a}-\vec{b}\right )\times \left (\vec{a}+\vec{b}\right )\right |^{2}+4\left (\vec{a}\quad .\vec{b}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \left |\vec{a}\times \vec{a}+\vec{a}\times \vec{b}-\vec{b}\times \vec{a}-\vec{b}\times \vec{b}\right |^{2}+4\left (\vec{a}\quad .\vec{b}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \left |2\left (\vec{a}\times \vec{b}\right )\right |^{2}+4\left (\vec{a}\quad .\vec{b}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 4\left (\vec{a}\times \vec{b}\right )^{2}+4\left (\vec{a}\quad .\vec{b}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 4\left |\vec{a}\right |^{2}\left |\vec{b}\right |^{2}=4.16.9=576$

solution.body:
Let $P(x_{1},y_{1})$ & $Q(x_{2},y_{2})$

$\therefore$ Roots of $2x^{2}-rx+p=0$ are $x_{1},x_{2}$

and roots of $x^{2}-sx-q=0$ are $y_{1},y_{2}$.

$\therefore$ Equation of circle $\equiv (x-x_{1})(x-x_{2})+(y-y_{1})(y-y_{2})=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}-(x_{1}+x_{2})x+x_{1}x_{2}+y^{2}-(y_{1}+y_{2})y+y_{1}y_{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}-\frac{r}{2}x+\frac{p}{2}+y^{2}-sy-q=0$

$\Rightarrow 2x^{2}+2y^{2}-rx-2sy+p-2q=0$

Compare with $2x^{2}+2y^{2}-11x-14y-22=0$

We get $r=11,s=7,p-2q=-22$

$\Rightarrow 2r+s+p-2q=22+7-22=7$

text:
Let $f:R\to R$ be a function defined by 

$f(x)=\left (2\left (1-\frac{x^{25}}{2}\right )(2+x^{25})\right )^{\frac{1}{50}}$. If the function $g(x)=f(f(f(x)))+f(f(x))$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to g(1) is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$f(x)=\left (2\left (1-\frac{x^{25}}{2}\right )\left (2+x^{25}\right )\right )^{\frac{1}{50}}$

and $g(x)=f(f(f(x)))+f(f(x))$

$\therefore$ $g(1)=f(f(f(1)))+f(f(1))$

Now, $f(1)=\left (2\left (1-\frac{1^{25}}{2}\right )\left (2+1^{25}\right )\right )^{\frac{1}{50}}$

$=\left (2\left (1-\frac{1}{2}\right )(2+1)\right )^{\frac{1}{50}}$

$=(3)^{\frac{1}{50}}$

$\therefore$ $f(f(1))=f\left (3^{\frac{1}{50}}\right )$

$=\left (2\left (1-\frac{\left (3^{\dfrac{1}{50}}\right )^{25}}{2}\right )\left (2+\left (3^{\frac{1}{50}}\right )^{25}\right )\right )^{\frac{1}{50}}$

$=\left (2\left (1-\frac{3^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}{2}\right )\left (2+3^{\frac{1}{2}}\right )\right )^{\frac{1}{50}}$

$=\left (2\times \left (\frac{2-\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )\left (2+\sqrt{3}\right )\right )^{\frac{1}{50}}$

$=\left [\left (2-\sqrt{3}\right )\left (2+\sqrt{3}\right )\right ]^{\frac{1}{50}}$

$=(4-3)^{\frac{1}{50}}$

$=1^{\frac{1}{50}}=1$

Now, $f(f(f(1)))=f(1)=3^{\frac{1}{50}}$

$\therefore$ $g(1)=f(f(f(1)))+f(f(1))$

$=3^{\frac{1}{50}}+1$

Now, greatest integer less than or equal to $g(1)$

$=[g(1)]$

$=\left [3^{\frac{1}{50}}+1\right ]$

$=\left [3^{\frac{1}{50}}\right ]+[1]$

$=[1.02]+1$

$=1+1=2$

text: Let A be a 3 $\times$ 3 matrix having entries from the set {$-$1, 0, 1}. The number of all such matrices A having sum of all the entries equal to 5, is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Case-I: 

$\begin{array}{ll} 1 & \to 7\text{times} \\  \\ \text{and}-1 & \to 2\text{times} \end{array}$

number of possible marrix $=\frac{9!}{7!2!}=36$

Case-II: 

$1\to 6$ times,

$-1\to 1$ times

and $0\to 2$ times

number of possible marrix $=\frac{9!}{6!2!}=252$

Case-III: 

$1\to 5$ times,

and $0\to 4$ times

number of possible marrix $=\frac{9!}{5!4!}=126$

Hence total number of all such matrix $A$ $=414$
